RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination Appeal
Member Name: Emerson Iverson
Member ID: W898477218
Reference Number: POC-007830134D-50943
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030)
Requesting Provider: Dr. [First Name] Duval, MD

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for my lower back disc surgery and decompression (CPT code 63030), as detailed in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03. The denial letter states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I am submitting this appeal to demonstrate that my diagnostic imaging findings are profoundly abnormal and directly correlate with my severe, debilitating clinical symptoms and physical examination.

Because a specific, branded Arkansas Medicaid medical policy for CPT 63030 was not made publicly available or attached to my denial, I have not quoted any official plan-specific policy criteria in this letter. However, standard national clinical guidelines for lumbar decompression and discectomy require objective imaging proof of nerve root compression that corresponds to the patient's neurological deficits, alongside a history of failed conservative therapy. My clinical records establish that I meet every standard clinical indication for this procedure.

1. Imaging Findings Demonstrating Clear Nerve Root Compression
My lumbar spine MRI, performed on 2026-05-26, demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and active compression of the traversing right L5 nerve root. These imaging findings are severe and provide clear, objective pathology that requires surgical decompression to relieve the mechanical pressure on my nerve root.

2. Direct Clinical Correlation with Imaging Findings
My physical symptoms and clinical examination findings directly match the pathology shown on my MRI:
- I suffer from intense, radicular pain radiating directly into my right calf, which is the exact anatomical distribution of the compressed L5 nerve root.
- Physical examinations performed by my surgeon, Dr. [First Name] Duval, reveal positive provocative testing on the affected right side.
- I exhibit a documented neurological deficit that corresponds precisely to the L4-L5 level and the traversing L5 nerve root.
- My functional capacity is severely limited; due to this nerve compression, I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have experienced 18 months of progressive, unrelenting lower back and leg pain that is completely unrelieved by rest.

3. Comprehensive Failure of Conservative Care
Surgical intervention is now the only viable option, as I have exhaustively completed and failed conservative, non-operative treatments:
- Supervised Physical Therapy: I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility from 2026-03-04 to 2026-06-24, totaling 16 visits. Despite my active participation, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note, my pain did not resolve.
- Medication: I have taken NSAIDs regularly for 6 months without achieving adequate relief.
- Interventional Therapy: I received a lumbar corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-04, which provided only 4 weeks of partial, temporary relief before my debilitating symptoms returned.

Additionally, there are no complicating clinical contraindications to this surgery; I have no active infections, no untreated substance use issues, a healthy BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The MRI from 2026-05-26 provides undeniable, objective proof of severe L4-L5 disc extrusion and nerve root compression that correlates perfectly with my right-sided radiculopathy and physical deficits. I urgently request that you review the enclosed MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, and clinical evaluations from Dr. [First Name] Duval, and reverse this denial so that I can proceed with this medically necessary surgery.

Please contact me or my provider if you require any further documentation. Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent medical matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Iverson
